notes:
Thin-content advice now names the case it cannot detect.

"This page has almost no content" comes with three remedies: write more, merge
it, or remove it. All three assume the page was meant to be an article. An index
is not — a category listing, an A–Z, a tag or author page does its job by
pointing elsewhere, and a low word count is normal.

Docket cannot reliably tell the two apart. Nine real pages were measured across
three different signals and every one of them overlapped, so no threshold was
invented. Instead the advice says so in a sentence, and says not to delete an
index page on the strength of its length.

The finding itself is unchanged. Those pages are thin, which is true.
